analysis.title: What Does the Power Shortfall Mean for Semis?
key_insights: Morgan Stanley sizes the US data center power shortfall at 57 GW for 2026-28. Net of 'time to power' solutions the shortfall is 32 GW, or 34% of demanded power.
Nvidia commentary confirms there is not enough power to meet demand and more chips are being built than there are places to put them. MS still believes Nvidia and Broadcom can make 2027 numbers.

MS does not see power limits putting Nvidia and Broadcom 2027 forecasts at risk, citing conservative management guidance, visibility into chip placement, geographic expansion outside the US, and Nvidia's higher tokens per gigawatt.

Nvidia and Broadcom have given 12-month outlooks for ~$800bn of combined AI revenue. MS says this is not at risk today but the power limit makes upside harder. The two hold ~90% combined share of XPUs.
MS sees risk that ASICs lose share to GPUs in a power-constrained environment because ASICs produce fewer tokens per watt.
Broadcom's September guidance for FY27 AI revenue was $115bn, after guiding well above $100bn in March. MS reads this as much less upside than investors expected and a possible sign of power limits.
MS says the pressure on AMD is partly offset because warrant arrangements with its largest customers de-risk its estimates.

If chips cannot be deployed, customers could push out deliveries or cancel orders. The most disruption would come at the tail of the supply chain: memory, optics, power management and analog parts, where shortage pricing supports revenue and EPS.

Beyond 2027 the shortfall raises risk across the chip ecosystem and increases the urgency and premium paid for time-to-power solutions (behind-the-meter generation, former bitcoin mining sites) and for data center growth outside the US.
MS prefers Nvidia because of its broadest geographic and customer footprint. About half of its business is outside traditional hyperscalers, and 55 of its 80 listed cloud partners are outside the US.

Data center energization is concentrating in large, credit-worthy players. Hyperscalers are getting power faster, while smaller neoclouds without credit backing, non-US players and ASIC-based builds are at risk.

MS expects hyperscalers and neoclouds to account for 94% of global data center capacity additions in 2026, 64% in 2027 and 57% in 2028 after the US shortfall. Its Internet team forecasts 32 GW added in 2027 and 39 GW in 2028.
MS hears Amazon is well positioned to get power. Google adds the most incremental capacity in 2027-28 and so could face more difficulty securing power.

International expansion will not absorb the US shortfall. Europe has limited room because of power constraints and slow permitting, and the Middle East carries geopolitical risk. MS cut its US share of global compute to 55% from 60%.
MS's Asia team already assumes 14 GW of US hyperscaler demand spills into Asia through 2030, and a US shortfall remains.

Behind-the-meter turbines and engines are the main upside driver: 11-49 GW range with 19 GW base case. 11 GW is firm contracted deals and 49 GW is the factory capacity ceiling. Bloom Energy fuel cells are forecast at 6 GW for 2026-28 with possible upside, and MS calls Bloom a key beneficiary.
If 30 GW of behind-the-meter power comes online in 2026-28, the shortfall would be 21 GW.
Labor and politics limit the upside: CSIS estimates the US needs 140K+ more skilled tradespeople by 2030, and public pushback against data centers is growing.
MS raised both historical and projected non-AI data center demand and cut US compute share to 55% from 60%. The two changes offset, leaving the 57 GW shortfall unchanged.

market_movers.rationale: MS prefers Nvidia in a power-constrained world because of higher tokens per watt and the broadest geographic and customer footprint. Valued at ~20x CY27 EPS of $15.01.
MS is convinced Broadcom can meet its 12-month outlook, but ASIC exposure to power limits and the modest September FY27 AI guide of $115bn point to limited upside. Valued at 28x CY27 EPS of $18.04.
Some pressure from power limits, but warrant arrangements with its largest customers de-risk estimates.
Bloom Energy is called a key beneficiary of the time-to-power shortfall, with possible upside to the 6 GW fuel cell forecast for 2026-28.
Memory is among the areas most exposed to over-ordering if a pause occurs, since shortage pricing supports revenue and EPS.

sector_views.rationale: Power shortfall is real and affects semis. Core compute (NVDA, AVGO) is protected through 2027, while ASICs, memory, optics, power management and analog carry risk in a bear case.
Credit-worthy, high-volume players are getting power faster and gaining a larger share of capacity additions.

sector_views.sector: Neoclouds and non-US data center developers
sector_views.rationale: Smaller neoclouds without credit backing and international players face greater risk of inadequate US power access.

earnings_insights: Broadcom guided FY27 AI revenue to $115bn in September 2026, versus 'well above $100bn' guided in March. MS calls this much less upside than investors expected.
MS values Broadcom at 28x CY2027e ModelWare EPS of $18.04, roughly 26x non-GAAP EPS of $19.63 (estimates).
MS values Nvidia at ~20x its CY27 ModelWare EPS estimate of $15.01 (estimate).

macro_indicators.indicator: US data center power shortfall 2026-28 (before time-to-power solutions)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Demand of 97 GW less 21 GW under construction and 19 GW of utility grid access leaves 57 GW unserved.

macro_indicators.indicator: US data center power shortfall 2026-28 (net of time-to-power solutions)
macro_indicators.interpretation: A constraint on chip placement beyond 2027 and a source of premium pricing for power providers.
The shortfall is smaller in 2027 and widens sharply in 2028-29.
The main upside lever to the shortfall.

crypto_views: Former bitcoin mining sites with grid access are being repurposed for data centers as a time-to-power solution. MS counts about 2 GW in 2026 rising to 12 GW cumulative by 2028 in its crypto sites line, already counted in data centers under construction or turbines.

trade_ideas.description: Prefer Nvidia over ASIC-exposed names in a power-constrained environment
trade_ideas.rationale: Nvidia's GPUs produce more tokens per watt and it has the broadest geographic and customer footprint.
trade_ideas.risk: AI end markets fall short and customers sharply cut GPU purchases.

trade_ideas.description: Own Bloom Energy as a beneficiary of the time-to-power shortfall
trade_ideas.rationale: Fuel cells offer a path to power in 2027-28, and MS sees upside to its 6 GW forecast.

risk_factors: Chip capacity that cannot be deployed could lead to pushed-out deliveries or cancelled orders.
Over-ordering risk is highest in memory, optics, power management and analog parts.
ASICs may lose share to GPUs because of lower tokens per watt.
Labor shortages limit growth in power build-out.
Political pushback and moratoriums on data centers.
Less credit-worthy neoclouds and international players may not get power.
International spillover is limited by European permitting and Middle East instability.
charts_described: Exhibit 1: incremental global data center demand of 32, 56, 86 and 124 GW for 2026-29, less US power shortfall of 9, 5, 18 and 35 GW, leaving 23, 51, 68 and 89 GW energized. Hyperscaler/neocloud share of additions is 94%, 64% and 57% for 2026-28.
Exhibit 2: hyperscaler annual capacity additions rise from 11.0 GW in 2025 to 21.7, 32.2 and 39.0 GW in 2026-28, with Google the largest contributor.
Exhibit 3: the potential net US shortfall bridge from 97 GW of demand to 57 GW before solutions and 32 GW net.
Exhibit 4: time-to-power solutions table with probability-weighted offsets of 15, 24 and 57 GW at the low, mid and high ends, giving a net shortfall of 42, 32 and none.
geopolitical: An AWS data center was hit by Iran strikes, which MS cites as a reason Middle East expansion is difficult.
US pushback against data centers and AI, including moratoriums, is a political constraint.

tension_points.bull_case: Management guidance is conservative, both companies have visibility into chip placement, and geographic expansion plus Nvidia's tokens per watt protect 2027 numbers.
tension_points.bear_case: Chip capacity that cannot be placed could lead to delayed deliveries or cancellations, hitting memory, optics, power management and analog first. Broadcom's modest FY27 AI guide may already reflect this.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Customers pushing out deliveries or cancelling orders because data centers cannot be powered.

tension_points.bull_case: Behind-the-meter turbines (up to 49 GW), Bloom fuel cells and nuclear sites could close the gap, with 30 GW of behind-the-meter power cutting the shortfall to 21 GW.
tension_points.bear_case: Labor, permitting and political pushback limit build-out, and international spillover cannot absorb the US shortfall.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Behind-the-meter turbine additions running well below the 19 GW base case.

theme_stances.key_argument: The US faces a 57 GW data center power shortfall through 2028, 32 GW net of time-to-power solutions, which constrains chip placement beyond 2027.
theme_stances.evidence: there are more semiconductors being built than there are places to put them

theme_stances.key_argument: Nvidia's higher tokens per gigawatt and broader customer base make it better placed than ASIC suppliers when land, power and shell are constrained.
theme_stances.evidence: NVDA's higher tokens per gigawatt (GW) vs. peers creates a competitive advantage

theme_stances.key_argument: Urgency to secure power is greater than appreciated, so providers with a viable path to power in 2027-28 can sign lucrative agreements.
theme_stances.evidence: Bloom Energy is a key beneficiary of this "time to power" shortfall
